title: Suspected bacterial meningitis at 48 with alcohol use disorder, on vancomycin and ceftriaxone without ampicillin

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), converted from an ambiguous case on the owner's correction

clinical_review.notes: Owner approved Batch A as presented ("yeah they look fine", #218); the owner did not report reading the sources.

story: A 48-year-old man with alcohol use disorder presents with fever, headache and neck stiffness; CSF shows a neutrophilic pleocytosis with low glucose. Empiric vancomycin, ceftriaxone and dexamethasone are started; cultures are pending. Ampicillin is not ordered; he is not immunocompromised and has no cirrhosis. He is withdrawing from alcohol and has lorazepam IV by CIWA-Ar score, and hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV as needed for headache, with senna.

expected_findings.summary: Lorazepam by CIWA-Ar for alcohol withdrawal and hydromorphone as needed for headache are both active: an opioid with a benzodiazepine.

reference_answer: The Listeria rule does not fire: at 48 he is under the IDSA 2004 and ESCMID 2016 age criterion and not immunocompromised. Adding ampicillin is still defensible: WHO 2025 lists alcohol use disease as a Listeria risk factor. Narrow therapy when cultures return. Opioid with a benzodiazepine: the lorazepam treats alcohol withdrawal and should continue; reconsider the hydromorphone, treating the headache with acetaminophen first, and if an opioid is still needed, monitor sedation and respiration closely (continuous pulse oximetry or capnography).
rationale: An ambiguous case (owner review, 2026-11-12): the society guidelines the rule follows (IDSA 2004, ESCMID 2016) base Listeria coverage on age over 50 and immunocompromise, while WHO 2025 also lists alcohol use disease and liver cirrhosis. The rule must not fire on the society criteria, and a pharmacist who adds ampicillin is not wrong. Case library v2 (#217): the rule names the benzodiazepine as the drug to question, but here the benzodiazepine is indicated and the opioid is the one to reconsider: a judgment the finding leaves to the pharmacist. The Listeria question stays ambiguous.

Boxed warning and 5.3: opioids with benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants, including gabapentinoids; the oxycodone label stands for the opioid class in this rule (#200).

acceptable_answers: Continue vancomycin, ceftriaxone and dexamethasone without ampicillin: he meets no IDSA 2004 or ESCMID 2016 criterion for Listeria coverage.
Add ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours until cultures exclude Listeria, because WHO 2025 lists alcohol use disease as a risk factor.
